in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! A 6-year-old child like Alex would fall within the eligible age range for Child Benefit (under 16).

Now, could you please confirm whether you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK actually. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are some specific circumstances where you may still be able to claim Child Benefit.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas), or are you living in a country that has a special agreement with the UK regarding benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it doesn't look like you would qualify for Child Benefit.

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. There are exceptions for certain circumstances, such as:

- Being a Crown servant posted abroad (e.g., a diplomat or member of the armed forces)
- Living in certain countries that have specific agreements with the UK

Since you've mentioned you're not a Crown servant and are simply living abroad with your family, you wouldn't meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit.

Just to confirm before I make my final assessment: Do you have any connection to the UK, such as recently moving from the UK, or do you have the right to reside in the UK? And does Alex live with you abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me abroad. We don't have any special connection to the UK at the moment, no.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on all the information you've provided, I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:**
To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. While Alex is within the eligible age range at 6 years old, you are currently living abroad and do not meet any of the exceptions that would allow you to claim from outside the UK. These exceptions include being a Crown servant posted overseas or living in certain countries with specific agreements with the UK.

**If your circumstances change:**
If you move back to the UK in the future and Alex continues to live with you, you would likely become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that point. You may also want to check your eligibility if you gain the right to reside in the UK through other means.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news. If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask.
